assets.scylla_heads.png: Create a truly transparent RGBA 1536x1024 2x2 sprite atlas for Nostos, ancient Greek Odyssey painterly pixel art. Four equal 768x512 cells, transparent clear gutters, all corners alpha 0, no backdrop, no bloom, no labels. SAME mythical Scylla sea monster head at far RIGHT of each cell, with a serpent neck trailing horizontally LEFT only a little (not whole body). Overhead high three-quarter action RPG camera, mouth opening toward RIGHT, silhouette readily readable when drawn 180 px wide. Head is long dark blue sea-hound with slate gray reptilian plates, uneven ivory teeth, dark blue gills, swept fins, small orange gold eyes. Creature has age and mass, Greek myth horror, clean pixelated brushwork and readable high contrast. In all four poses tip of snout at about x650, neck ends at x80, central at y250. Top left: low stalking head with closed mouth. Top right: neck thrust, jaws wide open. Bottom left: crooked head pulled back with open mouth. Bottom right: partially closed jaws from a slightly different angle. No blood, no people, no water splash, no light or shadows outside alpha silhouette. Fully transparent actual alpha, no checkerboard, no matte.
assets.cave_deck.png: 1536x1024 landscape finished cinematic background for Nostos Greek Odyssey 2D game, detailed hand-painted pixel art. From ON the deck of an ancient Bronze Age Greek oared galley, low three-quarter camera looking ahead, wood planks, stern beam and deck rails, a vertical mast and ropes offset to the right, no raised sails. Inside Scylla's narrow enormous marine cavern, imposing sculpted black basalt cliffs with dark teal reflections, a small sliver of fog-blue open water and dim natural sky forward, a soft amber light from out of frame on the foreground planks, cold mist in the distance. Dark but legible so wood, ropes and rocky walls are unmistakable, strong depth, large unobstructed lower foreground for adding 2D illustrated character sprites, polished game dialogue scene. No characters, no monster, no flames, no lanterns or torches, no lettering or UI. Restrained blue gray and sea-green palette, warm wood, solemn high contrast. Asymmetrical artful composition suitable for slow camera motion and close crops.
assets.open_deck.png: Edit this existing pixel art Greek galley background for the immediately following shot after the ship emerges from Scylla's cave. Keep the exact same viewpoint, ship deck, camera framing, mast, prows, ropes, wood texture, rail architecture and pixel-art style. Replace only the cave walls, rock arch and cavern with a wide expanse of gray-blue open sea and an overcast desaturated sky with a narrow pale dawn horizon. No islands, no land, no rock anywhere on the horizon. The solemn washed-out cold dawn has very little warm light, as if the torches have just gone out. Keep the existing rail silhouettes and deck continuity exact. No characters, no torches, no UI, no words.
assets.torch_bearers.png: Create one transparent RGBA sprite group of EXACTLY SIX anonymous adult Greek soldiers for Nostos, an illustrated ancient Odyssey pixel-art game. 1536x1024 wide landscape with the six full figures standing in a single continuous horizontal line across the full width; consistent eye level, roughly equal height. All dressed in the same bronze Greek soldier uniform: simple bronze helmets with cheek guards (helmets down, no faces emphasized), short dark red shoulder cloaks, bronze cuirasses, tan tunics, leather sandals and bronze greaves. Distinct believable subtle differences in age and posture, no heroes or recognizable named people. Each holds exactly one slim upright wooden torch in front of the body, with an UNLIT black cloth head reaching around forehead level. All six torch heads easy to locate and separated. Front three-quarter human-height camera, natural proportions, rich painterly pixel art with discrete brush marks, restrained burnt bronze, oxblood red and slate gray palette. No glow, no flames, no scenery, no floor, no text. All empty space and all margins are genuine alpha zero, transparent. Feet visible; no merged limbs.

cave_walls.prompt: One production environment atlas of four distinct rocky sea cave wall sections for a Greek Odyssey 2D game, 1536x1024 landscape, 2 by 2 equal cells, true transparent background with generous completely clear gutters. Above-water camera looking down about 35 degrees at the INNER face of a cave wall running diagonally back into a dark passage, tall vertical slate basalt strata with a jagged ledge, stalactites and little wet shelves at the foot. For ALL FOUR variants the rock mass is on the left and its irregular free water-facing edge is on the RIGHT; mirrorable in engine. Each prop fills 85 percent of its cell, its right edge dramatically shaped and base visible above water line. Upper-left close massive vertical basalt buttress and hanging ledge; upper-right sharply split sheer columns with a low shelf; lower-left tiered broken wet strata with an overhang; lower-right hooked stalactites joining a steep wall. Use sharply textured, finely painted pixel art, midnight blue-gray slate, wet neutral highlights on the exposed rock readable when put under torchlight, with strong depth between planes. NO water, no pool, no floor plane, no terrain behind individual pieces, no glow, no sunlight, no torch, no boat, no monster, no people, no labels. All four are distinct isolated scene props with everything outside them transparent. The attached art is a palette and material reference, it shows the game's cave from deck view; do not incorporate deck, railing or mast in the sprites.
